claims.proposition: Unique canonical fingerprints preserve reviewed hunks across matching changes, while ambiguous/new groups become ChangedSinceReview and notes separately become stale/orphaned/resolved.

evidence.exact_quote:
- [Review fingerprints](https://github.com/hewigovens/jayjay/blob/3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea/crates/jj-diff/src/review_fingerprint.rs), S00037 lines 10–15, 37–54, 92–153, 176–195, 259–288: canonical fingerprints use exact whitespace, uncollapsed/unhighlighted changes, side, source text, EOF-newline state and up to three unchanged context lines on each side. They omit absolute line/group positions and include an algorithm version; CRLF is retained in the hashed payload. Display groups are mapped back to canonical groups when whitespace is ignored.
- [Mark reconciliation](https://github.com/hewigovens/jayjay/blob/3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea/crates/jayjay-review/src/file_state.rs), S00015 lines 74–134, 194–235: matching identity/version has a fast path; otherwise a fingerprint inherits state only when unique in both previous and current snapshots. Ambiguous/new groups become `ChangedSinceReview`; removed reviewed groups remain counted. Legacy file/hunk marks and missing/version-mismatched snapshots use more conservative rules. Test assertions cover local edits preserving a sibling mark, moved context, duplicate fingerprints, removed reviewed groups, and whitespace-hidden groups (S00063 lines 58–165). These substantiate “matching hunks survive,” not automatic migration of every review mark.
- [Note reconciliation](https://github.com/hewigovens/jayjay/blob/3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea/crates/jayjay-review/src/reconcile.rs#L44), S00014 lines 44–69: resolved notes remain `Resolved`; no matching path in the current **diff** means `Orphaned`; a changed full file-pair identity means `Stale`; only then is the exact side/line/excerpt searched for `Current`. A file can still exist while its note is orphaned because that file no longer appears in the diff. The stored `anchor_context` is not used by this matcher (S00021 lines 15–47; S00083 lines 12–25). Notes do not use the hunk-fingerprint migration path. Provider file-read errors become missing replay data and therefore `Stale`, whereas summary/provider acquisition errors can propagate (S00016 lines 28–47; S00014 lines 31–35). A stale status alone does not prove a content edit.
- [Core review provider](https://github.com/hewigovens/jayjay/blob/3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea/crates/jayjay-core/src/repo/review_notes.rs), S00019 lines 35–71, 102–130, supplies both store-backed reports and the owned-note-vector entry point, using summary identity and rename-aware content. Replay uses the same diff/display pipeline and the note's recorded whitespace mode (S00016 lines 6–18, 28–47). The replay test explicitly produces `Some(0)` under the recorded ignore-whitespace mode and `None` under the other mode (lines 164–174). Integration-test assertions cover current/stale/orphaned/resolved states, equivalent owned snapshots and a note created on an already-renamed file (S00035 lines 74–188). The rename test is **not** proof that an existing note follows a later rename. The UniFFI `ReviewSession` wraps the same `ReviewStore` behind a mutex and supports JSON snapshots (S00064 lines 1–35).

Alternatives: bind repository and immutable revision provenance while allowing explicitly reconciled successors; or make change-level sharing intentional and visible. Verify exact commit selection and caller filtering before asserting isolation. Preserve current/stale/orphaned/resolved semantics; do not use hunk fingerprint survival as proof of note migration safety.

Keep pure reconciliation reusable without requiring this storage implementation. A native jj backup would not automatically include this external review file.

**Disposition.** Preserve the guard mechanism, with narrower wording: selected-path native conflict checks and current materialized old/new equality prevent specific stale-selection corruption. This is not an exact-operation precondition or a complete mutation lease.

**Primary evidence and supported lessons.**

- [guard.rs](https://github.com/hewigovens/jayjay/blob/3b53b4080f6704b4aad61b0173027b84ba0b10ea/crates/jayjay-core/src/repo/diffedit/guard.rs), S00003 lines 12–60: reject `Renamed` or any `old_path`; parse the selected path; require resolved native values in source **and parent** trees; compare current `Option<String>` against rendered `new_content`, then parent against `old_content`. The comments explicitly explain that unresolved conflicts can materialize as the same marker text and later be incorrectly written as resolved literal markers. Native conflict structure must be checked separately from display equality.

The public operation snapshots first under a working-copy lock, then guards both materialized sides and native conflict state and rewrites. Snapshotting may record an operation even if the later guard rejects. The lock used for snapshotting is finished before selection dispatch. The selection struct has no immutable revision/operation, mode or native metadata identity; ignore-whitespace is passed separately. Output metadata is taken from current source or parent.

Investigate: writer changes after validation; disk edits after the preliminary snapshot; metadata-only parent/source rewrites; current target resolution; changed whitespace toggle or diff projection after line selection; full/display mapping, CRLF/EOF and absent versus empty files. Preserve native conflicts distinctly from marker text. The parent tests inject stale content, all four destination checks use whitespace-sensitive mode, and unchanged file assertions do not prove unchanged op heads (S00043:72–142).

Alternatives: immutable revision/tree/shape and render-mode preconditions inside a serialized mutation boundary, retaining the materialized checks; or explicit re-render/reselection. Establish the actual before/after native operations on both rejection and success. Do not infer an exact-operation lease or retry safety from this guard alone. Upstream tests were inspected, not run.

Old removed lines contribute to selected/remaining results, explaining why an unchanged new side alone is insufficient. A parent **content** mismatch invalidates selection; a metadata-only parent rewrite with identical materialized selected-path sides need not. A complete, portable capture/restore protocol has **not** been established. This aggregate remains uncertain; five independent directions are extracted below rather than replacing or discarding it. The uncertainty concerns the protocol, not whether native state exists outside Git bookmarks.

| Commit backend and store selectors | [repo.rs](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/lib/src/repo.rs#L209), S00069 lines 219–261, 650–679, creates/loads `store`, `op_store`, `op_heads`, `index`, `submodule_store` with type selectors | Discover the actual backend and layout; a hardcoded Git-only folder list is not a generic backend export |
| Operations and views | [simple_op_store.rs](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/lib/src/simple_op_store.rs#L123), S00068 lines 123–155, stores separate `views/` and `operations/`; [op_store.rs](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/lib/src/op_store.rs#L248), S00071 lines 248–261, 358–380, stores visible heads/bookmarks/tags/remote views/Git refs, desired per-workspace commits, operation parents and rewrite predecessors | Native history and its referenced commit graph cannot be reconstructed from current bookmarks or an operation-log text listing alone |
| Publication heads | [transaction.rs](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/lib/src/transaction.rs#L125), S00075 lines 125–172, 202–240 | View, operation and index are written before publishing op heads. Unpublished operations can exist on disk without appearing at head. A manifest needs an explicit policy for retained operation roots and unpublished/unreachable data |
| Git objects and extra metadata | [git_backend.rs](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/lib/src/git_backend.rs#L228), S00010 lines 228–362 | Internal Git uses `store/git`; colocated/external backends persist `store/git_target`; `store/extra` is loaded independently. Copying only the workspace or only its backing Git directory can omit required state |
| Indexes | [default_index/store.rs](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/lib/src/default_index/store.rs#L225), S00088 lines 225–345, 519–554 | Default indexes can be rebuilt from retained operations, views and commit ancestry; missing/corrupt indexes trigger rebuild. They are a separate store but not necessarily irreplaceable bytes. Rebuild is conditional on complete underlying closure and applies to this backend, not every custom index |
| Workspace indirection | [workspace.rs](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/lib/src/workspace.rs#L369), S00067 lines 369–405, 568–630 | Secondary `.jj/repo` is a path file; paths are resolved from `.jj`, while `.jj/working_copy` stays local. The creation code prefers a relative path when possible. Absolute paths work through path-join semantics but need relocation treatment |
| Workspace path registry | [workspace_store.rs](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/lib/src/workspace_store.rs#L104), S00097 lines 104–128, 167–192, 233–250 | `repo/workspace_store/index` records workspace names and encoded paths, relative to repo path where possible, under its own lock. It is separate from operation views; a historical operation does not contain this physical path map. `load()` can initialize missing storage, so its name does not imply a side-effect-free read |
| Local checkout and tree state | [local_working_copy.rs](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/lib/src/local_working_copy.rs#L2580), S00070 lines 1155–1222, 2580–2626, 2646–2690; [schema](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/lib/src/protos/local_working_copy.proto), S00092 lines 19–78 | `checkout` records last-updated operation/workspace; `tree_state` records tree terms/conflict labels, file states, sparse patterns and Watchman state. - https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/lib/src/simple_op_store.rs (S00068:277–316): op/view retention follows supplied roots plus age, with acknowledged TOCTOU.

Define retained operation roots explicitly: current heads, selected historical operations, workspace checkout operations, and any intentionally retained unpublished/abandoned operations. Determine which objects remain available, rather than promising recovery of already-GCed history. Traverse relevant views and predecessor mappings, then tree/blob/conflict dependencies; preserve extras. A Git mirror can be a component of a backup but does not itself preserve jj operations/views or unsnapshotted files.

evidence.exact_quote:
The [Kaizen PR #216 diff](https://github.com/keanemind/jjk/pull/216.diff), local S00079 lines 17–45, corroborates `.jj/repo` path-file handling and corrects an operation-store watcher to use the resolved repo path. Its tests explicitly cover primary directory, secondary absolute path and secondary relative path (lines 80–125). This is an acquired PR patch, not proof of merge/release status or an executed test. Native jj source above is the stronger authority for layout. No retained child-note block was supplied beyond the handoff's evidence references.

**Git store closure and relocation.** `GitBackend::load` joins `git_target` against the jj store path and loads the Git repo plus `extra` separately (S00010 lines 335–362). `git_repo_at_workdir` checks shared `common_dir` identity (lines 390–410); `git_repo_path()` returns the Git administrative path, not necessarily every shared object directory (414–416). Windows relative targets are written with `/` for WSL compatibility; the code explicitly says an absolute target cannot work inside/outside WSL simultaneously (311–325). `canonicalize_git_repo_path` deliberately keeps the final `.git` component to avoid changing bare/worktree interpretation when following certain symlinks (605–617). Relocation needs to preserve those semantics rather than blindly canonicalize every path.

Backing Git can borrow object stores. [Git's repository-layout manual](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitrepository-layout), S00094 lines 221–236, 258–267, 405–427, specifies `objects/info/alternates`, Git environment alternates, `commondir`, shallow boundaries, submodule repositories and linked-worktree administrative data. Relative alternates are relative to the **object database**, whereas `commondir` is relative to the Git directory. These bases differ from jj's `git_target` and `.jj/repo` path bases.

This is also supported by the actual gix dependency rather than solely by generic Git documentation: jj declares gix 0.87.1 (S00080 line 63). The release tag resolves via S00106/S00110 to Gitoxide commit `3ebca8b66017ab2dd02a38f75f78f485bee1ded8`. Its repository opener uses `common_dir/objects` (S00096 lines 483–495), and [object-store loading](https://github.com/GitoxideLabs/gitoxide/blob/3ebca8b66017ab2dd02a38f75f78f485bee1ded8/gix-odb/src/store_impls/dynamic/load_index.rs#L233), S00115 lines 233–268, adds recursively resolved alternate paths to loose and packed object discovery. [Alternate resolution](https://github.com/GitoxideLabs/gitoxide/blob/3ebca8b66017ab2dd02a38f75f78f485bee1ded8/gix-odb/src/alternate/mod.rs#L41), S00116 lines 41–82, reads `info/alternates`, detects cycles and deduplicates canonical directories. Thus the handoff's negative jj literal search must not be interpreted as no alternates support. Exact nested-relative-path behavior and Git environment override parity are still open; the observed gix resolver joins parsed paths to its initial `objects_directory` (line 72), so a custom backup walker should not guess at equivalence. This is version-specific source inspection, not a restore trial.

- https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/lib/src/workspace.rs (local S00067:369–405, 568–630): `.jj/repo` can be a path file, relative to `.jj`; per-workspace working-copy state remains separate.
- https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/lib/src/git_backend.rs (S00010:228–362, 390–416, 605–635): internal/colocated/external Git; `store/git_target`; separately loaded `store/extra`; common Git directory identity; deliberately preserved final `.git` component; Windows/WSL relative-path handling and absolute-path limitation.
- https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/lib/src/repo.rs (S00069:219–261, 650–679): separate backend selectors and stores. Default submodule store is only a stub at this pin (S00093:22–51), not evidence of child-source closure.
- https://git-scm.com/docs/gitrepository-layout (S00094:221–267, 405–427): object alternates, shallow boundary, `commondir`, Git modules/worktrees and distinct relative path bases.
- https://github.com/GitoxideLabs/gitoxide/blob/3ebca8b66017ab2dd02a38f75f78f485bee1ded8/gix-odb/src/store_impls/dynamic/load_index.rs (S00115:233–268): actual loose/pack discovery includes alternate object directories. Its resolver recursively follows files and detects cycles (S00116:41–82).

Investigate a manifest that records each physical store once, logical references between them, the origin/base of each path, backend/version and unresolved/missing dependencies. Preserve internal, external, shared-worktree and symlink semantics on relocation. Do not infer closure by canonicalizing `git_repo_path()` alone. Verify dependencies in an isolated destination with original paths unavailable. Exact nested-relative alternates and Git environment override parity remain unresolved; the gix resolver's use of its initial `objects_directory` deserves explicit cases before writing a custom walker.

Alternatives: copy the entire resolved store graph with rewritten links; or materialize borrowed objects in a self-contained destination using a backend-aware export. The latter must preserve native metadata/history separately. No export or relocation implementation was executed.

evidence.exact_quote:
- `refs/jj/keep/*` protect commits from Git GC but are not the operation log. Creation/import can create per-commit refs; GC replaces these with index heads plus qualifying newer refs (S00010 lines 902–965, 1463–1474, 1558–1590; S00114 lines 636–637). The implementation therefore qualifies the prose “a ref for each commit in the operation log.” The default index rebuild walks operation ancestry, operation predecessor references and every view's referenced commits, then commit parents (S00088 lines 241–339). This is the concrete reason retained hidden/history objects matter beyond current visible heads.
- OpStore GC retains ancestors of supplied operation heads plus newer objects; SimpleOpStore explicitly notes a timestamp TOCTOU race (S00071 lines 481–488; S00068 lines 277–316). `jj util gc` defaults to two weeks and accepts `--expire now`, runs operation-store GC followed by GitBackend GC (S00076 lines 26–67). GitBackend recreates keep refs, GCs extra-table segments and invokes Git GC (S00010 lines 1558–1590, 970–987). The ref timestamp check also documents re-import races (929–937). These are mitigations and retention rules, not a backup GC fence.
- Test source corroborates removal of redundant keep refs and retention varying with index/time (S00108 lines 156–250); extra-table GC removes unreachable segments while keeping the reachable segment contents (255–310). These tests do not certify a concurrent backup. No test was run here.

**Physical workspace state and capture consistency.** [Working-copy documentation](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/docs/working-copy.md), S00005 lines 9–29, 69–110, describes snapshotting and shared/stale workspaces. The view records what *should* be checked out; local state records the last completed update (S00071 lines 258–261). Dirty bytes, untracked/ignored files and sparse omission are separate facts. `WorkingCopyFreshness::check_stale` distinguishes updated, stale and sibling operations and can regard differing operation IDs as fresh when the tree still matches (S00072 lines 348–399). Operation-ID inequality alone is not a complete stale-state classification.

`LocalWorkingCopy::start_mutation` locks one workspace's state and reloads its checkout/tree after acquiring the lock (S00070 lines 2662–2690). Finish writes tree state and checkout state separately (2940–2965). Operation publication, extras tables, workspace registry, Git GC and ordinary file writes are distinct boundaries. A working-copy lock does not stop arbitrary editor writes or freeze all workspaces/external stores. An unchanged operation head before/after capture would not alone prove dirty-file consistency.

Also, acquiring a `ReadonlyRepo` is not proof that discovery was nonmutating: `RepoLoader::load_at_head` can reconcile divergent heads by merging operations (S00069 lines 714–736); missing/corrupt indexes can be rebuilt (S00088 lines 528–554); workspace-store loading can initialize files (S00097 lines 116–125). Exact-operation loading avoids head reconciliation but can still need an index. Preserve the captured heads and actual local state before choosing any repair or normalization.

**Competing evidence, rather than a blanket rejection of filesystem copying.** The pinned [README](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/README.md#L102), S00112 lines 102–121, calls safe concurrent replication experimental and says rsync/Dropbox results should not be corrupt. The linked [concurrency document](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/blob/e9f48b3e4c1c5e816fbbfbfd06c154a6a96b0215/docs/technical/concurrency.md#L40), S00117 lines 40–62, qualifies this: working copies may mismatch, Git backend corruption is possible in known scenarios, and colocated replication is not thoroughly tested and might lose bookmark pointers. It offers reindexing for its linked historical bug; that is not proof that every capture defect can be repaired. The implementation's distributed-extras race above is another limit. `test_bad_locking` simulates merging two copied repositories and checks both child heads plus a merge operation; an interrupted op-head publication test checks recovery without a new operation (S00113 lines 104–162, 168–199). Neither covers live multi-store capture with concurrent GC, alternate stores and dirty workspaces. Preserve replication/merge as a real native design direction, with conflicts and recovery semantics; do not equate it with a verified exact-point backup.

**Alternatives, unresolved questions and aggregate extraction.** A coordinated offline copy or storage snapshot of the entire discovered dependency set could be a baseline; a live capture would need demonstrated ordering/barriers and retention protection across all relevant writers/stores. These are alternatives to investigate, not certified recipes. A logical backend-aware export could omit rebuildable caches only if it preserves selected historical operations, referenced commits/trees/blobs, native metadata and separately captured workspace state. No complete all-store export or live capture protocol was established by the reviewed APIs; this is a bounded evidence statement, not a claim that none exists anywhere.

Investigate nonmutating discovery and capture under a barrier spanning native repo writers, every affected workspace, editor/file writers and external/alternate store GC. An equal head ID before/after is insufficient for dirty files or expiring unreachable data. Do not hold an undocumented collection of locks and assume it constitutes a fence.

Alternatives: stop relevant writers and take a coordinated copy; storage-level snapshots covering every dependency; or a logical immutable-object export with explicit roots and independently captured workspace files. Evaluate native replication as a different recovery model that may merge operations and report conflicts. Define crash/interruption behavior and verify captured closure before resuming writers. No live protocol is certified by this review.

Define retained operation roots explicitly: current heads, selected historical operations, workspace checkout operations, and any intentionally retained unpublished/abandoned operations. Determine which objects remain available, rather than promising recovery of already-GCed history. Traverse relevant views and predecessor mappings, then tree/blob/conflict dependencies; preserve extras. A Git mirror can be a component of a backup but does not itself preserve jj operations/views or unsnapshotted files.

Do not equate the two-week default GC grace period (`cli/.../util/gc.rs`, S00076:26–67) with a capture fence. Independent Git GC and alternate-store GC must be addressed. Tests inspect keep-ref reduction and extra-segment collection (S00108:156–310); they are not backup tests and were not executed here.

Alternative: carry all store bytes under a coordinated snapshot, or export selected reachable closure plus explicit retention receipts. Default index rebuilding is possible if source closure exists; missing history cannot be repaired by merely rebuilding an index. Keep aggregate uncertainty until restoration of retained historical states is demonstrated.

Investigate manifests carrying workspace identity, physical root mapping, checkout operation, desired view commit, actual files and sparse/conflict metadata as separate observations. Missing paths or an unavailable workspace cannot be silently reconstructed from its desired commit and called a capture of its dirty state. Decide explicit inclusion for untracked/ignored files and initialized nested repositories. Preserve deletions, empty files, executable bits, symlinks and sparse omissions distinctly.

Relocation may invalidate stored paths, file-stat shortcuts and filesystem-monitor clocks. Verify resumed scanning on an isolated copy instead of assuming old cache state is portable. Snapshotting live files with an ordinary jj command changes native history; it is an alternative capture policy only if explicitly intended, not a way to relabel preexisting dirty files as already committed. No native operation was created during this review.
